_comment: Fleet schedule. Edit, then run: bash bin/apply-config.sh

heartbeat._what: One relay check for every agent. Hand an agent a random number, it must reply with that number plus one, then pass it on — a correct reply is only possible if the previous value arrived.
heartbeat._cost_note: Once a day, not every 30 minutes. Measured 2026-08-02: one full relay costs ~960s of wall clock. At 1800s it occupied over half of all wall-clock time on a four-core machine, and the fleet's own load average reached 20 — five times the cores. The relay answers one question (can the agents pass a message), the answer changes rarely, and re-asking it hourly was the single largest consumer of a machine that has none to spare.
heartbeat._load_note: Skip the run when the 1-minute load average is above this. The check costs 2.4 microseconds against the 960 seconds it guards — the cheapest thing on the board protecting the most expensive. Agents timing out under load is not a comms failure, and recording it as one is how three councils ended up diagnosing the wrong thing.

watchdogs._what: Run each monitored project's own test suite.

self_improve._what: Mine session transcripts, propose tooling, commit only what survives.

pipeline._what: Closes the rota's loop: unprocessed proposals are implemented by claude on rota/* branches in worktrees, pytest runs, hermes (a different vendor) reviews each diff, and the board lists what awaits a human merge. One cycle drains the queue — up to 12 builds — rather than taking one and leaving the rest; at one proposal an hour from the rota, taking one every two hours meant the backlog only ever grew. Nothing merges itself.

council._what: Agents take turns proposing workflow improvements. They read the board, decide for themselves, and write to a shared transcript. Nothing is applied — a human reads and decides.
council._cost_note: Each turn is one agent for ~20-100s, one at a time. Four agents x two rounds is roughly 8 turns — double what it was. Every 3 hours still keeps the machine alone between sessions. ollama is the expensive one: dolphin-llama3 holds several GB resident while it thinks, on a box with 8. If the load gate starts deferring everything, drop ollama first and rounds second.
council._vendor_note: claude=anthropic, hermes=openai, openclaw=openai, ollama=local. openclaw shares a vendor with hermes, so it adds a voice but not an independent one; ollama is the only genuinely different training here and the only one that keeps working with the wifi off. Two of four agreeing across vendors is a much stronger claim than two agreeing within one.
council._ollama_note: In the council: no, on this hardware. Measured across 20 turns (2026-08-05): median 169s, worst 712s, and ONE turn in twenty that was its own thought — the rest echoed a prompt heading, copied the worked example verbatim, or critiqued a line of its own input. Three prompt rewrites did not move it. qwen2.5:3b was tried on the same brief: 564s and a fragment. A council turn needs ~1,500 tokens of context, and prefill on this 4-core box runs ~5 tok/s, so the reading alone costs minutes before a word is generated. The reason to want a local voice is unchanged — it is the only one that survives the wifi dropping — so ollama stays RUNNING and stays in the chat pane, where a human asks a direct question and can wait. It is out of the council, where it cost 3-10 minutes a sitting and contributed once.

e2e._what: End-to-end check against live infrastructure, with canaries proving each path was actually traversed. Includes real agent turns.
e2e._cost_note: Two agent turns per run. Daily is enough to catch drift; hourly would spend turns to learn nothing new. The --quick variant runs on every merge via githooks/post-merge and costs nothing.

rota._what: One agent at a time, in rotation, reads the board and answers three questions: what would improve this machine, what would help Marsita the Ultra, what would help the planet. Proposes only — never applies. Continuous on the NUC: the next turn starts 60s after the previous one finishes, so one agent is always working and two never overlap.
rota._cost_note: Hourly, one agent per firing — not all three. A turn is 20-170s and one core, so the hourly cost is a few percent of one core, against the relay's 960s. Three agents means each one's turn comes round every three hours, and the load gate defers a turn rather than taking it on a saturated machine: a turn spent timing out is recorded as the agent having nothing to say, which is the failure this fleet already made twice.

board_medic._what: Probes the board on :8787 every five minutes; two silent probes trigger a fleet-server kickstart, a failed revival raises needs_you. The heartbeat medic, applied to the board itself.

local_voice._what: One short question a day to the local model, so the offline fallback is known-good before the day the wifi dies. It is not an agent here: this laptop is too slow for local inference as work (measured 2026-08-05 — a council turn cost 3-10 minutes and said nothing). It is a backup with a pulse.
